record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: A compact space Y is called co-Namioka if for every Baire space X and every separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R there exists a dense G_delta set A in X with A × Y contained in C(f). A space Y is a Hahn space with respect to R if for every topological space X and every horizontally almost separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R, the set C_Y(f) = {x in X : {x} × Y is contained in C(f)} is residual in X. Which co-Namioka compact spaces are Hahn spaces with respect to R?

evidence.quote: Recall that a topological space Y is called co-Namioka if for each Baire space X and each separately continuous function f : X × Y → R there exists a dense Gδ-set A in X such that A × Y ⊆ C(f).

We say that a topological space Y is a Hahn space with respect to a topological space Z if for each topological space X and each horizontally almost separately continuous function f : X×Y → Z the set CY (f) = {x ∈ X : {x}×Y ⊆ C(f)} is residual in X.
Problem 7.2. Characterize those co-Namioka compacts which are Hahn spaces (with respect to R).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let all topological spaces be Hausdorff. For a function f: X × Y → ℝ, let C(f) denote the set of points of joint continuity of f. A function f: X × Y → ℝ is called separately continuous if for every fixed x ∈ X the map y ↦ f(x,y) is continuous on Y and for every fixed y ∈ Y the map x ↦ f(x,y) is continuous on X. A function f: X × Y → ℝ is called horizontally almost separately continuous if for every y ∈ Y the map x ↦ f(x,y) is continuous on X, and for every x ∈ X the map y ↦ f(x,y) is continuous on Y at all but possibly countably many points (more generally, on a residual set).

A compact space Y is called co-Namioka if for every Baire space X and every separately continuous function f: X × Y → ℝ there exists a dense G_δ subset A ⊆ X such that A × Y ⊆ C(f).

A topological space Y is called a Hahn space with respect to ℝ if for every topological space X and every horizontally almost separately continuous function f: X × Y → ℝ, the set
   C_Y(f) := { x ∈ X : {x} × Y ⊆ C(f) }
is residual in X.

Problem: Characterize those compact spaces Y which are co-Namioka and which are also Hahn spaces with respect to ℝ. Equivalently, give an internal topological characterization of the class of compact Hausdorff spaces lying in the intersection of these two classes.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search yields literature on co-Namioka compact spaces (Eberlein, Corson, Valdivia compacta, σ-fragmentable C_p(Y), etc.) and on Hahn spaces, but no source reporting a complete characterization of those co-Namioka compacta that are Hahn spaces with respect to ℝ. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Namioka spaces and strongly Baire spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Study of Namioka-type properties; no characterization of co-Namioka Hahn compacta given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on Namioka-type spaces does not resolve the characterization.

status_evidence.title: The Namioka property of KC-functions and Kempisty spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Kempisty/Hahn-type continuity properties without supplying the characterization sought.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization of co-Namioka Hahn compacta is provided.

status_evidence.title: Separate and joint continuity - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of separate vs joint continuity results; lists classes of co-Namioka compacta but no Hahn characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference does not state a solution.
